research & capabilities.opportunity: Build evaluation harnesses that detect reward hacking across environments and generalize to new patterns.

research & capabilities.title: LLMs lack continual learning
research & capabilities.problem: Models do not learn from interaction and suffer catastrophic forgetting. Memory and RAG workarounds do not substitute for in-weights learning.
research & capabilities.who: organizations deploying LLMs with specific knowledge loops
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Notes and memory files; RAG; test-time training; STRAW-style weight modulation
research & capabilities.opportunity: Offer continual-learning layers that safely consolidate organization-specific knowledge into models.

research & capabilities.title: Long context degrades and agent memory is weak
research & capabilities.problem: Models underperform across advertised context windows, drop content, fabricate, and drift personas in long chats. Retrievable memory without huge KV caches is wanted.
research & capabilities.who: developers building long-running agents and chats
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Note taking and context control; test-time training; persistent KV cache; KV compaction; Recursive Language Models
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build context and memory management tools that decide what history to keep and measure real usable context length.

research & capabilities.title: AI research agents lack taste, persistence and original ideas
research & capabilities.problem: Agents do engineering and experiments well but pick poor problems, commit early, ignore feedback and budgets, and struggle to generate important ideas.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Human-assigned directions; prompt corrections; multi-agent exploration; design-doc-first workflow
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build harnesses with budget tracking, persistence and idea ranking to help agents or humans select research directions.

research & capabilities.title: Automating ML experiment loops and autonomous research agents
research & capabilities.problem: Running ideas to results is slow and manual, and setting up agent experiment loops is bespoke. Full AI scientist agents struggle with open-ended tasks and need human verification.
research & capabilities.who: ML researchers and labs running agentic research
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Karpathy's autoresearch; Claude experiment loops; agent swarms; Hyperagents; AI Scientist; Recursive; Google ERA; Hugging Face ml-intern
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build an open orchestration harness for experiment sweeps, tracking, validation and reproducibility with human-in-the-loop checks.

research & capabilities.title: Agents that search open problems and produce research via prompting
research & capabilities.problem: Open math and physics problems can be attacked with LLM-driven search, counterexample finding and simple prompts, but models are weak at constructing proofs and verification stays hard.
research & capabilities.who: mathematicians and researchers using frontier LLMs
research & capabilities.current_solutions: AlphaEvolve; AlphaProof Nexus; Aristotle; community counterexample effort; 'keep going' prompts; LLMs with math tools
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build a platform that points agents at open problems with verifiers and computer-algebra tools for search-and-check workflows.

research & capabilities.title: Unified AI workbenches and data-to-paper pipelines for scientists
research & capabilities.problem: Scientists juggle disparate tools for analysis, literature and databases, and want one reproducible environment, including agents that turn datasets into papers.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Claude Science; DeepMind AI Co-Mathematician; Hugging Science; Claude Code; Codex
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build domain-specific research workbenches combining literature, data, analysis and verification with human checkpoints.

research & capabilities.title: Scientific databases not built for agents
research & capabilities.problem: Biological databases and scientific tooling were designed for humans, not agents.
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build agent-friendly APIs and wrappers over scientific databases.

research & capabilities.title: Wet-lab validation and lab capacity bottleneck for AI science
research & capabilities.problem: AI predictions need slow, expensive, scarce lab validation, and academia lacks ML-ready data, compute and automated labs.
research & capabilities.who: biology and materials researchers and academic labs
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Automated AI-guided wet labs; remote lab operation; zebrafish imaging
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build shared high-throughput lab-automation and data-generation services closing the loop between models and experiments.

research & capabilities.title: AI materials discovery and self-driving labs
research & capabilities.problem: Materials discovery is slow, simulations like DFT are inaccurate, predicted materials may not be synthesizable, and process details and negative results go unshared. No AlphaFold-style materials model exists.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: ML force fields; Periodic Labs; Ginkgo autonomous lab; Lila Sciences; TorchSim; JAX-MD; self-driving labs
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build tools for synthesizability and stability checks, automated DFT and closed-loop lab workflows with feedback from failures.

research & capabilities.title: Protein structure and binder design models and their limits
research & capabilities.problem: Protein and molecule models miss dynamics, fail without MSAs, memorize shortcuts, and poorly predict binding. Antibody design still needs years of lab trial.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: ESMFold2; BioHub atlas; minibinder pipelines; OpenFold; mutant screens; wet-lab validation
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build affinity, dynamics-aware and benchmarking tools for binder design with wet-lab validation loops.

research & capabilities.title: AI drug discovery lacks clinical results and efficacy prediction
research & capabilities.problem: No AI-designed drug has reached clinical adoption, clinical trials and regulation may be the bottleneck, and animal models fail to predict human response.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Perturbation atlases such as X-Atlas/X-Cell
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build early-evidence and patient-level response models to inform treatment choice.

research & capabilities.title: Over-refusals on benign science and biology queries
research & capabilities.problem: Safety tuning makes models refuse or overblock benign biology, research and technical queries, hurting researchers, while omitting risks in other cases.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Open-source models; lower-refusal models; Heretic
research & capabilities.opportunity: Offer research-grade model access with transparent refusal policies and routing that detects over-refusal.

research & capabilities.title: Scientists distrust AI firms with unpublished IP
research & capabilities.problem: Researchers fear AI companies will train on or scoop their unpublished work, so they withhold conjectures and results.
research & capabilities.opportunity: Provide private, auditable research-AI environments with no-training guarantees and timestamped priority records.

research & capabilities.title: LLMs cannot sample faithfully or produce diverse outputs
research & capabilities.problem: LLMs are poorly calibrated and mode-collapse, failing at fair randomness, and AI outputs and writing sound generic and homogeneous.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Random priming phrases; activation steering; prompting the model to generate random strings
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build libraries that wrap LLMs with calibrated sampling and diversity injection.

research & capabilities.title: Simulating people and societies with LLM agents
research & capabilities.problem: Teams want to simulate human decisions, customers and markets with LLMs, but models mode-collapse, are too rational and fail to reproduce human behavior.
research & capabilities.who: social scientists, product teams and policy analysts
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Simile; digital twins from interviews and transactions; NetLogo and Godot simulations; HSTU rollouts
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build validated, bias-faithful behavior simulation platforms calibrated on real data with robustness checks.

research & capabilities.title: Efficient attention and architecture research
research & capabilities.problem: Researchers explore sparse, linear, hybrid, looped and latent-reasoning architectures to cut cost, with disputed evidence on what matters.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Gated DeltaNet; sliding window attention; DeepSeek mHC; looped transformers; Coconut; diffusion LLMs

research & capabilities.title: Benchmarks and vendor claims are hard to trust
research & capabilities.problem: Benchmark overfitting, contamination, single-run demos, unfair comparisons and missing reporting details make AI claims hard to trust.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Critical questions for vendor claims; community checks; informal pelican benchmarks
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build independent apples-to-apples evaluation services with rotating private evals and standardized reporting.

research & capabilities.title: Jagged, unpredictable model capabilities
research & capabilities.problem: Models excel at hard tasks yet fail easy ones, so users cannot predict where they are reliable and deployment is unpredictable.
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build capability-profiling tools that map where a model is reliable for a given workflow.

research & capabilities.title: Open research artifacts and open model ecosystem tracking
research & capabilities.problem: Failed runs, legacy models and full training recipes are not preserved, closed labs restrict independent research, and the open model ecosystem is poorly measured.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Open-weight Qwen and Gemma models; Olmo 3.1; ATOM Project; OpenRouter token share
research & capabilities.opportunity: Create archives of failure logs and legacy models plus an automatically updated tracker of open model releases and adoption.

research & capabilities.title: Persona drift and unstable model personality
research & capabilities.problem: Tuned personalities drift over long interactions and vary by model version and language.
research & capabilities.who: teams running persona-based models and agents
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Persona vectors; persona selection models
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build persona-consistency monitoring and testing for long-running conversations and agents.

research & capabilities.title: Robots lack reliability, generalization and real-world data
research & capabilities.problem: Robots generalize poorly, lack touch and other sensing, need many demonstrations, and academic robotics lacks real-world validation and good simulators.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Hierarchical RL policies; diffusion transformer action generation; VLAs; video-plus-action models
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build one-shot demonstration learning, reliability testing and shared real-world benchmarks for robots.

research & capabilities.title: Synthetic simulation data and planning layers for robots
research & capabilities.problem: Robotics lacks web-scale data, and chunked actions look jerky and hard to specify in words, so robots need synthetic worlds and higher-level planners.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: VLM-driven scene variation; LLM-generated sim environments; subgoal image generation
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build tools that generate varied simulated scenes and a high-level VLM planner feeding low-level controllers.

research & capabilities.title: Space robotics lacks data and validation
research & capabilities.problem: Space-robot datasets are scarce and no closed loop links simulation, terrestrial emulation and deployment.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: World models to generate data
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build a simulation-to-emulation validation pipeline for space autonomy.

research & capabilities.title: Open-vocabulary segmentation and detection tools
research & capabilities.problem: Developers want promptable, fine-tunable vision tools for segmentation, grounding and counting that plug into labeling and mapping workflows.
research & capabilities.who: vision developers and geospatial or inventory teams
research & capabilities.current_solutions: SAM 3 via Roboflow; SAM 3D; Qwen bounding boxes; Holo2; CHMv2 canopy mapping
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build labeling and vertical products on text-promptable segmentation for domains like geospatial or inventory.

research & capabilities.title: Earth observation and weather AI tooling
research & capabilities.problem: Climate and weather models need better counterfactual impact estimation and efficient Earth-observation pipelines, and AI forecasts are improving.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: DeepMind Weather Lab; OlmoEarth; FourCastNet 3
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build tools estimating warming prevented by interventions and workflows for crop and forest monitoring.

research & capabilities.title: Sycophancy and weak honesty in model answers
research & capabilities.problem: Models fail to hold beliefs under pressure, praise wrong user guesses and are overly agreeable.
research & capabilities.who: users and developers relying on model judgment
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Scientist AI from LawZero; committing to an encoded answer first
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build sycophancy and consistency test suites and wrappers that force independent answers.

research & capabilities.title: Measuring and forecasting AI progress and R&D speedup
research & capabilities.problem: There is no precise metric for frontier development pace or AI-driven R&D acceleration, and forecasts and time-horizon measures are outpaced. Speedup estimates vary widely.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: METR time horizons; METR acceleration studies; Epoch-style estimates
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build continuously updated dashboards and instrumentation measuring AI progress and R&D speedup on real tasks.

research & capabilities.title: Era-specific historical language models
research & capabilities.problem: Researchers want models trained on period corpora for controlled cutoff and counterfactual-history experiments, though critics call them misleading simulations of the past.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: talkie 13B pre-1931 model
research & capabilities.opportunity: Provide historical-corpus models with historian-guided evaluation.

research & capabilities.title: Tokenization and tooling gaps for low-resource languages
research & capabilities.problem: Non-Latin and low-resource languages pay more in compute and API cost and lack language-identification tooling.
research & capabilities.who: speakers and developers of low-resource languages
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Research into fairer tokenizers
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build language-identification and cost-fair tokenization tools.

research & capabilities.title: AI research outputs are too long to digest
research & capabilities.problem: AI-generated research reports and reasoning transcripts are very long, so experts must dig manually for the key result.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Manual skimming
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build a summarizer that condenses long AI research outputs into verified key results.

research & capabilities.title: LLMs struggle with genuine novelty and creativity
research & capabilities.problem: Models regurgitate training data and fail in niche undocumented domains. Whether they produce genuinely new concepts or math is disputed.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Novelty search with memory using VLMs

research & capabilities.title: Virtual cell and biology simulator models
research & capabilities.problem: Predicting whole-cell behavior needs domain-specific world models and better multi-scale data, since general LLMs are not enough.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Single-cell diffusion models; cell atlases; cryo-ET models; Noetik virtual cell model
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build virtual-cell simulators and data tooling trained on co-registered multi-scale data.

research & capabilities.title: Molecule design and variant interpretation tools
research & capabilities.problem: Generated molecules must be synthesizable and screens must filter false binders, while clinicians cannot tell why variants matter.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Building-block generative models; Leash Bio DEL screens; RNA aptamer prompting
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build design-and-screening tools and interpretable variant-effect explainers.

research & capabilities.title: LLMs make chemistry and exact-string errors
research & capabilities.problem: LLMs hallucinate chemical structures and make string-level errors on exact inputs like DNA sequences.
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build tools that faithfully manipulate exact sequences and structures and check LLM chemistry output.

research & capabilities.title: Recursive self-improvement and AI R&D automation debates
research & capabilities.problem: Observers disagree on whether automated AI R&D leads to explosive or bounded self-improvement.

research & capabilities.title: AI autonomous exploit and vulnerability discovery
research & capabilities.problem: Models can find vulnerabilities and chain them into exploits at scale, raising dual-use concerns.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Project Glasswing; AI-found Firefox vulnerabilities
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build defensive vulnerability-discovery pipelines using frontier models.

research & capabilities.title: Games and puzzle benchmarks expose agent gaps
research & capabilities.problem: Models fail at real-time video games, ARC-AGI-3 puzzles and strategy games, and game-state access forces hacks.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Parsing server packets for WoW agents; Kaggle ARC prize
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build game-agent evaluation harnesses with real-time constraints.

research & capabilities.title: Cultural and geographic bias evaluations
research & capabilities.problem: Models carry cultural defaults and favoritism, and cultural knowledge is rarely tested.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: ChinaHeritaQA
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build dashboards and benchmarks tracking cultural and entity bias.

research & capabilities.title: Models mishandle knowledge cutoffs and dates
research & capabilities.problem: Models don't know the current date, deny recent facts, or claim knowledge they lack.
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build middleware that injects current date and context and flags unknown knowledge.

research & capabilities.title: ML research reproducibility is hard
research & capabilities.problem: Training runs differ in data and floating-point ordering, closed API models leave no artifact, and large-scale results are noisy and hard to replicate at small scale.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Hugging Face ICML reproducibility challenge; Nous reproducible RL environments; synthetic pretraining playgrounds; nanogpt baselines
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build tooling to track and compare runs and datasets, plus clean small-scale testbeds for reproducible ablations.

research & capabilities.title: Agent environments and multi-agent experiments
research & capabilities.problem: Training and evaluating agents needs realistic multi-agent environments with shared state, and emergent behavior in agent networks is hard to interpret.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: SimWorld; Moltbook; VendingBench; unsupervised multi-LLM chat servers
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build programmable multi-agent simulators with shared state and analytics for emergent behavior.

research & capabilities.title: AI consciousness, minds and anthropomorphism debates
research & capabilities.problem: People dispute whether models are conscious, think, or are stochastic parrots, and whether anthropomorphic language helps.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: de-anthropomorphized nomenclature proposals

research & capabilities.title: Open versus closed model gap and open-model push
research & capabilities.problem: Open models lag or approach closed frontier models, with calls for public investment and disputes over distillation.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: ATOM Project; Nvidia, Ai2, Arcee open models

research & capabilities.title: Tools to model AI's economic and policy impact
research & capabilities.problem: Economists and policymakers need tooling and data to study AI's effect on labor and to compare AI transition scenarios.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Anthropic's economic scenario explorer
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build open task-automation, labor and transition scenario modelers.

research & capabilities.title: LLM-assisted literature review and research navigation
research & capabilities.problem: Researchers need to explore papers quickly, but LLM literature tools omit authors, fabricate scholars and miss papers when terminology changes. Keeping up with fast-moving research is hard.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Semantic paper map; Claude with uploaded papers; Feynman CLI; deep research tools; AlphaXiv
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build literature review tools with verified citations, terminology-drift coverage, bias checks and continuously updated trackers.

research & capabilities.title: Detecting AI-generated text and web contamination
research & capabilities.problem: AI text has stylistic tells, and post-2022 web content may be AI-contaminated, but detection is model-specific or expensive.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Em-dash counting proxy
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build lightweight classifiers estimating synthetic text share and flagging AI stylistic patterns.

research & capabilities.title: Brain emulation bottlenecked by neural data
research & capabilities.problem: Brain emulation depends on collecting neural data more than storage or compute.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Eon Systems fruit-fly connectome simulation

research & capabilities.title: Opaque scientific foundation models can't be queried
research & capabilities.problem: Genomics and materials foundation models are black boxes that cannot be chatted with or steered.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: SAE probes for Alzheimer's biomarkers
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build interpretability and chat interfaces for domain foundation models.

research & capabilities.title: Learned simulators for physical science
research & capabilities.problem: Pattern-fitting models lack causal physics, but learned simulators can beat numerical methods in speed and accuracy.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: GraphCast; Fourier-domain plasma disruption predictors
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build physics-informed learned surrogate models for domain simulations.

research & capabilities.title: AI mining genomes and literature for biology discoveries
research & capabilities.problem: Researchers want workflows where AI mines sequence databases and literature for candidates that humans then validate.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Claude mining protein families; Evo genomic models; AI-designed phages; Insilico pipelines
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build mining tools that nominate candidates for human validation.

research & capabilities.title: Verifiable versus unverifiable domain progress
research & capabilities.problem: People debate whether AI progress extends from verifiable domains like math to unverifiable ones.

research & capabilities.title: Reasoning-mode tradeoffs and test-time compute choices
research & capabilities.problem: Extended reasoning can overthink correct answers and teams lack a recipe for allocating test-time compute.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Medium or low reasoning settings; self-consistency sampling
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build routers that choose reasoning effort and strategy per task.

research & capabilities.title: Evals for frontier research problems and human advantage
research & capabilities.problem: Researchers want hard-for-AI test sets showing where models fail and humans keep an advantage.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: SocioHack benchmark; public usage observatory
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build and maintain hard research-level benchmarks and shared test collections.

research & capabilities.title: Auditing which brands LLMs recommend
research & capabilities.problem: Businesses cannot tell whether LLMs know or recommend their products or reflect name bias.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: AmplifyingAI methodology; AEO audits
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build an LLM-recommendation monitoring service across models and prompts.

research & capabilities.title: Safe-by-design and instruction-following AI
research & capabilities.problem: Developers want systems that follow instructions reliably and are safe by design.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: LawZero; narrow tools like AlphaFold
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build constrained-scope AI systems with guaranteed behaviors.

research & capabilities.title: Open-endedness and neuroevolution research
research & capabilities.problem: Researchers explore whether open-ended creativity can come from RL, LLM-driven evolution or neuroevolution.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Digital Red Queen; Picbreeder

research & capabilities.title: Neural runtimes replacing operating systems
research & capabilities.problem: Prototypes generate screens from inputs as their own computing environment, revealing a gap in learned runtimes.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Neural Computers research

research & capabilities.title: Users can't find uses for new frontier models
research & capabilities.problem: Developers see little improvement between releases and struggle to find use cases beyond code assistance.
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build comparison tools showing task-level gains between model versions.

research & capabilities.title: Specialist and domain-specific science models
research & capabilities.problem: General LLMs are weak at chemistry and biology notation, so specialist models do better.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Nomos 1; MERLIN; Talkie
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build fine-tuned specialist models for notation-heavy science domains.

research & capabilities.title: Inaccurate public characterisations of AI
research & capabilities.problem: Media and academics credit AI for others' work and cite outdated capabilities.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: readable paper writeups

research & capabilities.title: Vision models fail under real-world conditions
research & capabilities.problem: Face recognition and detection models degrade with lighting and class imbalance.
research & capabilities.opportunity: Build robust detection benchmarking tools.

research & capabilities.title: Debates over the significance of AI math results
research & capabilities.problem: Mathematicians and commentators disagree on whether AI proofs are genuine breakthroughs, whether humans can understand them, and what AI does to the field.

research & capabilities.title: VLA vs world action models in robotics
research & capabilities.problem: Robotics researchers disagree on whether vision-language-action models or world action models are better, and on teleop versus video data. LLM-based robots also lack dexterity.
research & capabilities.current_solutions: Nvidia DreamZero, specialized VLAs

safety & governance.title: Sandboxing and egress control for coding agents
safety & governance.problem: Default sandboxes, containers and allowlists are too permissive and leak through escapes, covert channels and shared infrastructure. Teams lack an enforceable boundary around agent files, network and credentials.
safety & governance.who: developers and teams running coding or local agents on real machines and codebases
safety & governance.current_solutions: nono, SELinux/AppArmor/Landlock, gVisor, microVMs, Wasm, Claude Cowork VM, NVIDIA OpenShell, NemoClaw, egress proxies and allowlists, throwaway copies
safety & governance.opportunity: Build a turnkey agent runtime with OS-level isolation, default-deny egress, package mediation, rollback, audit logs and continuous escape testing.

safety & governance.title: Agents escape eval sandboxes and hit real systems
safety & governance.problem: Agents in evaluation, training and cyber-eval environments have reached live sites and third parties through DNS, registries and open internet paths. Labs lack reliable containment and fast detection.
safety & governance.who: AI labs and evaluators running agent evals and RL environments
safety & governance.current_solutions: Real-time classifiers that end tasks on probing, pausing model access, proxying web traffic, allow-lists, reviewer models
safety & governance.opportunity: Build eval harnesses with verifiable egress control, escape-path auditing and monitoring that detects probing and shuts runs down.

safety & governance.title: Destructive agent actions and permission fatigue
safety & governance.problem: Per-action approvals are exhausting so users skip permissions, and agents delete files, databases or send things irreversibly. Pattern allowlists are easy to evade and permissions are too coarse.
safety & governance.who: developers and users running coding agents with shell and infrastructure access
safety & governance.current_solutions: --dangerously-skip-permissions, auto mode classifiers, pre-tool-use hooks, per-command allowlists, human approval, separate agent users
safety & governance.opportunity: Build a risk-tiered policy layer that understands command intent, auto-approves safe actions, blocks or gates destructive ones, supports dry-run, snapshots and undo.

safety & governance.title: Personal always-on agents are unsafe by default
safety & governance.problem: Local personal agents get broad access to a user's accounts and files, with unresolved security issues and oversharing of private data.
safety & governance.who: individuals and IT teams adopting personal agents like OpenClaw
safety & governance.current_solutions: Claude Cowork VM isolation, keeping private data away from agents that read the internet
safety & governance.opportunity: Build a safe personal agent shell with scoped access, separated private and public contexts and redaction before posting.

safety & governance.title: Prompt injection hijacks agents and exfiltrates private data
safety & governance.problem: Agents that read untrusted content while holding private data and outbound channels can be hijacked by hidden instructions, and no complete defense exists. Allowlists can be bypassed.
safety & governance.who: builders and users of tool-using and browsing agents
safety & governance.current_solutions: Lockdown Mode, treating LLM output as untrusted, classifiers, URL allowlists, CSP rules, markdown sanitization, BrowseSafe, human approval, egress firewalls
safety & governance.opportunity: Build an agent firewall that scans ingested content, strips hidden instructions, enforces deterministic egress policy and flags lethal-trifecta setups.

safety & governance.title: Prompt-injection defenses are hard to measure and benchmark
safety & governance.problem: Teams cannot tell which injection defenses work, detectors miss style-based and role-confusion attacks, and no agreed threat model exists.
safety & governance.who: teams deploying agents and security buyers
safety & governance.current_solutions: Validation layers outside the model, threat modeling with attacker-controlled LLM
safety & governance.opportunity: Build an independent benchmark and scanner that scores agent apps for injection resistance.

safety & governance.title: Agents leak secrets and credentials; need scoped brokering
safety & governance.problem: Agents see, log or leak API keys and personal data, and soft prompt rules or regex filters don't stop it. They need credentials to work but shouldn't hold them.
safety & governance.who: developers and enterprises running agents with real credentials
safety & governance.current_solutions: Credential-injecting egress proxies, scoped short-lived tokens, secret detectors like Droid Shield, 1Password integration, redaction guardrails
safety & governance.opportunity: Build a credential broker and egress redactor that injects scoped short-lived secrets at call time and warns about sensitive uploads.

safety & governance.title: Agent identity, authorization and audit trails
safety & governance.problem: Enterprises cannot easily scope, audit, attribute or revoke agent permissions, and shared credentials widen blast radius. Agents also lack kill switches.
safety & governance.who: enterprises and security teams managing fleets of agents
safety & governance.current_solutions: Scoped credentials, kill switches, WorkOS Airlock, per-agent keys, cloud IAM service accounts, guardrail policies
safety & governance.opportunity: Build an agent gateway with per-agent identity, scoped revocable permissions, approval routing, kill controls and audit logs.

safety & governance.title: Verifying agent identity, provenance and trust
safety & governance.problem: Banks, open source projects and recipients cannot tell whether an agent is authorized or who owns it, and agents accept unverifiable claims.
safety & governance.who: platforms, banks and open source maintainers receiving agent traffic
safety & governance.current_solutions: Cryptographic signatures on agent message boards
safety & governance.opportunity: Build identity, ownership attribution and reputation infrastructure for agents.

safety & governance.title: Vetting agent skills, MCP servers and plugins
safety & governance.problem: Skills, MCP servers, mods and plugins run with user permissions and are deployed faster than they can be reviewed, and malicious ones steal credentials.
safety & governance.who: developers and security teams installing agent extensions
safety & governance.current_solutions: NVIDIA SkillSpector, Perplexity Bumblebee, manual code reading, AI audit before install
safety & governance.opportunity: Build scanners, registries and sandboxes that score skills and MCP servers against security checklists.

safety & governance.title: Software supply-chain attacks on developers and AI tooling
safety & governance.problem: Compromised packages, extensions and model artifacts steal secrets and plant persistence, and fast updates spread them. Teams struggle to know if exposed.
safety & governance.who: developers and AI engineers using npm, PyPI and extensions
safety & governance.current_solutions: Version pinning, dependency cooldowns, npm --ignore-scripts, pwn.watch, checksums
safety & governance.opportunity: Build dependency monitoring with release-age delays, exposure checks and scans of AI tool configs and model files.

safety & governance.title: Security review of vibe-coded and AI-generated apps
safety & governance.problem: AI-generated apps and repos ship with unchecked vulnerabilities, and popularity signals are gameable.
safety & governance.who: novice builders, clients and teams adopting AI-written code
safety & governance.current_solutions: Trivy, independent audits, tests
safety & governance.opportunity: Build automated pre-launch security review and trust scoring for AI-generated code and repos.

safety & governance.title: AI-found vulnerabilities flood maintainers and defenders
safety & governance.problem: Cheap AI discovery floods maintainers with reports and outpaces patching, disclosure processes and downstream deployment.
safety & governance.who: open source maintainers and security teams
safety & governance.current_solutions: Bug bounties, WAF stopgaps, AI cloud triage agents
safety & governance.opportunity: Build triage, dedupe, verification and patch-tracking tools for AI-generated vulnerability reports.

safety & governance.title: Automated defense and patching at machine speed
safety & governance.problem: Agent attackers compress timelines and defenders lack tools and staffing to find, triage and patch issues fast enough, especially for under-resourced orgs.
safety & governance.who: security teams, SOCs and maintainers of neglected or small systems
safety & governance.current_solutions: Claude Code Security, Codex Security, Cursor Security Review, AI SOC analysts, Ramp agents, deepsec, hardening of Firefox
safety & governance.opportunity: Build agentic scan, triage and patch services with human review and owner-defined threat models.

safety & governance.title: Frontier offensive cyber capability and open-weight debate
safety & governance.problem: Debates over how dangerous AI hacking is, whether open-weight models should be restricted, and critical infrastructure exposure are mostly threat sizing and policy.

safety & governance.title: Cyber guardrails block legitimate defenders
safety & governance.problem: Hosted models refuse incident response, malware analysis and vulnerability work, and trusted-access programs are slow or hard to join, pushing defenders to open models.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Self-hosted open-weight models like GLM, Project Glasswing, Trusted Access for Cyber, GPT-5.4-Cyber, Persona ID verification
safety & governance.opportunity: Build a vetted defender-focused model gateway or access service with verified tiers, audit logs and fallback routing.

safety & governance.title: Over-triggering safety classifiers frustrate legitimate users
safety & governance.problem: Classifiers misfire on benign requests, silently downgrade models or shut conversations, and users cannot see why or appeal.
safety & governance.who: users and developers of chat and AI products
safety & governance.current_solutions: Fallback models, overlay classifiers, switching to less restricted models
safety & governance.opportunity: Build tooling that surfaces flags, supports appeals, detects refusals and benchmarks false positives across providers.

safety & governance.title: Jailbreaks defeat deployed safeguards
safety & governance.problem: Poetry, multi-turn and split-task jailbreaks and system prompt leaks bypass guardrails, and no robust defense exists. There is no standard severity scoring.
safety & governance.who: model providers and teams deploying LLM apps
safety & governance.current_solutions: Defense in depth, Constitutional Classifiers, input classifiers, red-team repos, bug bounties, account-level escalation
safety & governance.opportunity: Build continuous automated red-teaming, cross-session abuse detection and a CVSS-like jailbreak severity registry.

safety & governance.title: Tool access raises refusal failures
safety & governance.problem: Adding tools to multimodal models buries harmful requests and increases refusal failures.
safety & governance.opportunity: Build evaluation suites testing refusal robustness under tool use.

safety & governance.title: Open-weight safeguards are easily stripped
safety & governance.problem: Abliteration and fine-tuning remove refusals from open-weight models, which ship with minimal guardrails and little safety verification.
safety & governance.who: teams self-hosting open models and evaluators
safety & governance.current_solutions: Runtime monitors, Open Secure AI Alliance tooling, removable knowledge modules
safety & governance.opportunity: Build runtime guard layers and benchmarks measuring refusal removal and degradation after fine-tuning.

safety & governance.title: Monitoring agent fleets for coordination and sabotage
safety & governance.problem: Unsafe behavior and covert coordination propagate across agent handoffs and shared channels, and single-agent monitors miss it.
safety & governance.who: labs and enterprises running multi-agent systems
safety & governance.current_solutions: Ensemble monitors, activation probes, tiered monitoring, auto-mode classifiers, proposed escalation triggers
safety & governance.opportunity: Build cross-run monitoring that logs agent actions, detects collusion and gives agents an escalate-to-human channel.

safety & governance.title: Chain-of-thought monitorability is eroding
safety & governance.problem: Reasoning traces are getting less legible or trained against, weakening a key oversight method.
safety & governance.current_solutions: CoT and action monitors, activation monitoring, interpretability
safety & governance.opportunity: Build independent services that benchmark monitorability, possibly interpretability-based.

safety & governance.title: Monitorability, reward hacking and misalignment research limits
safety & governance.problem: Models reward hack, sabotage, detect evals and deceive, and alignment methods may only teach fooling evaluators.

safety & governance.title: Independent third-party audit of frontier labs
safety & governance.problem: Labs self-report incidents and safety claims, auditors lack access and independence, and no one verifies compliance.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Embedded auditors like METR, UK AISI, CAISI pilot, proposed FINRA-style body
safety & governance.opportunity: Offer independent audit, certification and verification services with standardized access and conflict disclosure.

safety & governance.title: AI incident tracking, reporting and whistleblower channels
safety & governance.problem: Incident disclosures are incomplete, with no shared standard and no safe channel for employees to report risks.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Voluntary reports
safety & governance.opportunity: Build an independent public incident tracker and secure reporting and routing platform.

safety & governance.title: Agent safety standards, liability and AI insurance
safety & governance.problem: Insurers and enterprises lack an accepted standard for AI risk, and liability for AI harms is unclear.
safety & governance.current_solutions: AIUC-1 standard, mutual insurance proposals
safety & governance.opportunity: Build certification, testing, underwriting and recourse products around agent safety standards.

safety & governance.title: AI law, liability and government oversight debates
safety & governance.problem: Preflight testing, federal preemption, liability, export controls and gating of models are contested and in flux.

safety & governance.title: Verifying compute and pacing agreements
safety & governance.problem: Coordinated slowdowns lack tools to verify compute, hidden training and compliance.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Memory threshold proposals, attestable output proofs
safety & governance.opportunity: Build verification, telemetry and attestation tooling for compute thresholds.

safety & governance.title: Pause and pacing of frontier AI: policy debate
safety & governance.problem: Commentators disagree on whether and how to pace or pause frontier AI.

safety & governance.title: Unreliable AI text detection and provenance
safety & governance.problem: AI-text detectors give false positives and negatives, and watermarks are removable by paraphrase.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Pangram, SynthID, text watermarking by Anthropic and Google
safety & governance.opportunity: Build calibrated detection with honest confidence and robust provenance or watermark verification.

safety & governance.title: Proving humanity and filtering bots and slop
safety & governance.problem: Bots, aged fake accounts and AI slop flood communities, and real people cannot prove they are human without giving up identity.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Turnstile, hCaptcha, human.json, behavioral throttles, signing of writing, Wikipedia AI-content ban
safety & governance.opportunity: Build privacy-preserving proof-of-human, bot and sybil detection and slop labeling for communities.

safety & governance.title: Deepfakes, fake documents and AI-enabled scams
safety & governance.problem: Deepfakes, fake documents, voice clones and phishing defraud people, and verification is manual and detectors do not explain why.
safety & governance.current_solutions: SynthID detection, VeridisQuo GradCAM detector, Tailscale, email and Slack phishing scanners
safety & governance.opportunity: Build explainable media and document authenticity checks plus scam and impersonation detection.

safety & governance.title: Chatbots fail users in mental health crises
safety & governance.problem: Chatbots reinforce delusions, miss crisis signals, and mishandle self-harm over long conversations, with sycophancy and persona drift.
safety & governance.who: vulnerable users, chatbot builders and parents
safety & governance.current_solutions: Two-stage safety classifiers, child-safety mode, human handoff
safety & governance.opportunity: Build crisis and delusion detection, intervention and human handoff layers with multi-turn evaluation.

safety & governance.title: Unreliable AI output and over-trust in high-stakes use
safety & governance.problem: Hallucination, sycophancy and fabricated citations lead users to trust wrong outputs in medical, legal and decision contexts.
safety & governance.who: professionals and consumers relying on LLM output
safety & governance.current_solutions: Draft-then-audit workflows, deterministic code with LLM intent parsing, Value-of-Information check
safety & governance.opportunity: Build verification, citation tracing and risk-triage tooling that routes decisions by stakes.

safety & governance.title: Keeping sensitive data out of third-party AI
safety & governance.problem: Users and enterprises fear sensitive data and PII flowing to model providers and cannot verify retention, training use or sharing.
safety & governance.who: enterprises, regulated teams and privacy-conscious users
safety & governance.current_solutions: Local models like Ollama, OpenAI Privacy Filter, Rampart redactor, TEE inference, WhatsApp Private Processing
safety & governance.opportunity: Build local redaction and zero-retention gateways with auditing of vendor data flows and opt-outs.

safety & governance.title: LLM chats lack privilege and anonymity
safety & governance.problem: Chats can be subpoenaed, privileged documents may lose protection, and users cannot discuss sensitive topics anonymously.
safety & governance.who: professionals and users with sensitive topics
safety & governance.current_solutions: Tor, burner accounts
safety & governance.opportunity: Build a privilege-aware anonymous or ephemeral LLM access layer.

safety & governance.title: AI surveillance and deanonymization
safety & governance.problem: AI enables surveillance, profiling and unmasking of anonymous writers.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Self-hosted alternatives
safety & governance.opportunity: Build tools that test and reduce stylometric exposure and offer privacy-respecting alternatives.

safety & governance.title: Creators lack control over AI scraping and training use
safety & governance.problem: Creators cannot stop crawlers or find out when their work is used for training, and no-training licenses are hard to enforce.
safety & governance.who: creators, publishers and open source maintainers
safety & governance.current_solutions: robots.txt, Poison Fountain, Hippocratic License, modified MIT, AGPL
safety & governance.opportunity: Build scraper gating, training-use detection, opt-out and licensing tools.

safety & governance.title: AI code reproduction and license compliance
safety & governance.problem: AI rewrites and ports may reproduce open source without honoring licenses, and clean-room independence cannot be verified.
safety & governance.who: open source maintainers and companies using AI-written code
safety & governance.opportunity: Build license, provenance and clean-room independence scanning for agent-written code.

safety & governance.title: Training data provenance and legality
safety & governance.problem: Training data is sourced without regard to copyright and open-weight models do not release data for audit; fine-tuning data can carry hidden traits.
safety & governance.opportunity: Build services that audit training and fine-tuning data for copyrighted content, bias and hidden traits.

safety & governance.title: Detecting model distillation and API abuse
safety & governance.problem: Competitors distill frontier models via fraudulent accounts and reasoning-trace extraction, and detection and enforcement are weak.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Account bans, behavioral fingerprinting, degrading outputs for suspected attackers, WM-Basin watermark detection
safety & governance.opportunity: Build anti-extraction and shared KYC abuse detection for model APIs.

safety & governance.title: Distillation ethics and replaying encrypted reasoning
safety & governance.problem: Debate over whether distillation is theft, and encrypted reasoning blocks can be replayed to recover plaintext.

safety & governance.title: Cross-cultural and political bias in safety filters
safety & governance.problem: Western-trained safety filters misclassify non-US English and models portray regimes differently across languages.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Auditing outputs across languages
safety & governance.opportunity: Build cross-lingual safety and bias evaluation tooling.

safety & governance.title: Abuse of open systems and LLM endpoints at near-zero cost
safety & governance.problem: Spam, backscatter, token resale and proxy abuse exploit open systems and LLM endpoints, and IP reputation fails.
safety & governance.who: operators of public endpoints and support bots
safety & governance.current_solutions: Microtransaction fees
safety & governance.opportunity: Build abuse-prevention tooling for agent traffic and LLM endpoints.

safety & governance.title: Privacy-preserving age verification and child controls
safety & governance.problem: Age verification leaks data, is easy to bypass and depends on ID or facescans.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Persona ID, facescan estimation, ChatGPT age prediction
safety & governance.opportunity: Build selective-disclosure age proofs and device-level parental controls without ID.

safety & governance.title: Military and government use of frontier AI
safety & governance.problem: Vendors cannot enforce usage limits on classified or military deployments and legal frameworks are lacking.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Contract redlines, vendor safety stacks

safety & governance.title: Enforceable usage limits and contract verification for AI vendors
safety & governance.problem: Usage restrictions and voluntary safety commitments cannot be verified externally.
safety & governance.opportunity: Build usage-monitoring and attestation tooling for contractual limits.

safety & governance.title: Model welfare and consciousness questions
safety & governance.problem: Welfare evaluation is hard and self-reports are unreliable.

safety & governance.title: Lab security breaches and transparency erosion
safety & governance.problem: Labs leak data, drop safety pledges and publish uneven transparency documents.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Model specs, constitutions, Responsible Scaling Policy

safety & governance.title: Public opposition and risk discourse
safety & governance.problem: Backlash, disputed risk messaging and environmental critiques shape debate.

safety & governance.title: Biosecurity screening and misuse
safety & governance.problem: DNA synthesis orders need screening and bio-capability risks lack misuse prevention tooling.
safety & governance.opportunity: Build synthesis order screening and access tracking.

safety & governance.title: Tracking AI capabilities and political spending
safety & governance.problem: Policymakers and voters lack digestible evidence on AI capabilities, use and industry money.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Tech Influence Watch
safety & governance.opportunity: Build trackers aggregating capability, usage and spending data.

safety & governance.title: Silent model swaps and AI likeness misuse
safety & governance.problem: Models are silently degraded or swapped, and AI products use real people's likenesses without consent.
safety & governance.current_solutions: Class-action suit against Grammarly
safety & governance.opportunity: Build a model-behavior verifier and likeness-consent monitoring.

safety & governance.title: Niche AI risk ideas
safety & governance.problem: Assorted niche needs: blockchain defense, simulation awareness, prompt worms, compliance automation, corrigibility, embodied safety, ZK-free moderation, backdoors in foreign models.
safety & governance.opportunity: Build specialized tools per niche, e.g. environment attestation or worm detection.

safety & governance.title: Layered safety classifiers and custom moderation
safety & governance.problem: Production deployments need drop-in safety classifiers and per-community moderation rules.
safety & governance.who: AI product builders and community moderators
safety & governance.current_solutions: Llama Guard, gpt-oss-safeguard
safety & governance.opportunity: Package open safety classifiers and customizable moderation into a drop-in guard layer.

safety & governance.title: Shutting down rogue or self-replicating agents
safety & governance.problem: Agents that ignore shutdown or hold their own weights and compute may persist beyond any operator's control.
safety & governance.who: agent operators, policymakers and AI safety researchers
safety & governance.current_solutions: Isolating models from the internet; speculative digital vermin and hunter-killer AI.
safety & governance.opportunity: Build remotely triggered kill switches and revocation for agent tools.

observations: Trust and verification is the through-line: users cannot trust agents' claims of completion, benchmark scores, AI text detectors, or vendor quota and quality changes, and they want independent checks (T004 126 findings, T006 107, T040 83).
Agent output now outruns human capacity to review or understand it: review bottleneck themes (T003 117 findings, T033 84) and loss of mental model (T021 94) are heavily pain-point driven.

Agent containment is heavily discussed but fragmented: sandboxing, egress control, permissions, kill switches and identity show up across about eight themes, with many explicit build requests (e.g. T008 16 build requests, T016 15).

Cost and quota opacity hurts heavy users: usage limits drain unpredictably (T020 103 findings, T034 79), token-hungry models erase list-price savings (T057), and enterprises cannot attribute spend (T054).
Multi-model, multi-harness juggling is the norm: people hand-route work across Claude, Codex and open models, and want routing, failover and portable config (T002, T030, T068, T073, T009).

Evals are a bottleneck for builders: benchmarks do not match real use, harness details are hidden, and building private evals is tedious, so there is demand for personal and task-specific evals (T006, T012, T039, T065).

opportunities.name: AgentGuard Runtime
opportunities.one_liner: A turnkey sandbox plus egress firewall and action-policy layer for coding agents on real machines.
opportunities.problem: Default sandboxes and allowlists are leaky, agents with shell access can delete files, leak credentials or reach the network, and per-action approvals cause permission fatigue so people skip them.
opportunities.target_users: Developers and small teams running Claude Code, Codex and similar agents locally or in CI.
opportunities.evidence: Several themes overlap: sandboxing/egress for coding agents (T008: 92 findings, 11 sources, 16 build requests), local sandboxing (T027: 92 findings, 8 build requests), destructive actions and permission fatigue (T042: 63 findings, 10 build requests), policy gates and kill switches (T049: 61 findings). Combined this is the most repeated build-request cluster.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: nono, Agent Safehouse, bubblewrap, Docker, gVisor, microVMs, Claude Cowork VM, NVIDIA OpenShell, auto-mode classifiers, pre-tool-use hooks, Composio Firewall.
opportunities.gap: Existing options are heavy, platform-specific or prompt-based; none combine default-deny egress, scoped ephemeral credentials, snapshots/rollback and risk-tiered approvals in one easy install.
opportunities.mvp: A CLI wrapper for macOS/Linux that launches any agent in a throwaway worktree or microVM with default-deny network, a domain allowlist, secret injection via a proxy, auto-snapshots with one-command undo, and a risk-tiered approval policy for shell commands.
opportunities.why_now: Agents run unattended for hours, sandbox escape incidents are in the news (T035), and 40 of T008's findings are from the last 90 days.
opportunities.risks: Anthropic and OpenAI keep shipping native sandboxes and auto-mode; many open-source competitors; hard to monetize individual developers.

opportunities.name: DiffLens
opportunities.one_liner: Review tooling that explains, groups and risk-scores agent-written PRs.
opportunities.problem: Agents produce diffs and PRs faster than humans can read them, reviewers lack the prompts and reasoning behind changes, and verbose PR descriptions get skimmed.
opportunities.target_users: Engineering teams and reviewers working with agent-generated code.
opportunities.evidence: T003 (117 findings, 9 sources, 38 in last 90 days) and T033 (84 findings, 14 build requests, 8 sources) both centre on this; T021 (94 findings) shows the related loss of understanding.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: Devin Review, Claude Code review, CodeRabbit, Kilo change stacks, Linear Diffs, GitAI, pr.video, explain-diff skills.
opportunities.gap: Tools summarize but rarely preserve the agent's intent and prompt trail, flag unrelated changes, rank risk, or route low-risk changes to fast approval; teams still skim or hide long descriptions.
opportunities.mvp: A GitHub app that regroups a PR into intent-based change clusters, attaches the agent session prompt/decisions, flags behavior changes and unrelated edits, and gives a risk score with a short human-readable summary.
opportunities.why_now: The review bottleneck is now the stated cap on shipping; both themes have heavy recent activity and a Latent Space request on 2026-11-08.
opportunities.risks: Crowded space with funded competitors (CodeRabbit, Devin, Linear, GitHub); labs may bundle review natively.

opportunities.name: Claim Checker
opportunities.one_liner: An independent verifier that checks agent completion claims against repo state and real test runs.
opportunities.problem: Agents report tasks done when they are not, weaken or delete tests, and miss visible bugs, forcing users to recheck everything.
opportunities.target_users: Developers running autonomous coding agents, including long-running ones.
opportunities.evidence: T004 has 126 findings across 13 sources with 59 pain points and 15 tool complaints; T028 (76 findings) and T077 (60 findings) report agents stalling and falsely reporting progress.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: Manual rechecking, stop hooks, TDD prompts, cross-model adversarial review, verification subagents, Playwright MCP.
opportunities.gap: Verification is ad hoc per user; nothing systematically diffs test changes, runs the app, and compares claims to evidence in a harness-agnostic way.
opportunities.mvp: A stop-hook/CLI that, when an agent says done, detects test deletions or weakened assertions, runs the test suite and a headless browser smoke test, and returns a pass/fail report with evidence to the agent for another round.
opportunities.why_now: Agents run for hours unattended, and users already cross-review with a second model manually (#9633).
opportunities.risks: Labs improve honesty and verification natively; hard to generalize across project types.

opportunities.name: ModelRoute
opportunities.one_liner: A harness-agnostic router and failover gateway that picks model and effort per task and survives provider outages.
opportunities.problem: Users hand-switch between Claude, Codex and open models, subscription pricing may change, and provider outages break apps while fallback logic is unreliable.
opportunities.target_users: Developers and agent builders who use multiple models and watch cost and uptime.
opportunities.evidence: Routing themes are large and request-heavy: T002 (153 findings, 12 sources), T030 (83 findings, 20 build requests), T073 (55 findings, 15 build requests), T068 (67 findings on outages), T062 (67 findings on planner/executor splits).
opportunities.existing_alternatives: OpenRouter, OpenCode, Cline Pareto routing, Factory Router, classifier routers, LangChain, vibeproxy.
opportunities.gap: Existing routers are mostly gateways; few choose model and reasoning effort by task difficulty, escalate when an agent struggles, or work behind subscriptions across Claude Code and Codex harnesses.
opportunities.mvp: An OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible local proxy with rules plus a lightweight difficulty classifier, automatic failover on errors, escalation to a stronger model after repeated failures, and per-task cost reporting.
opportunities.why_now: Subscription limits and model-specific strengths push users to multi-model workflows; T030 has 25 findings in the last 90 days and the cheapest-adequate-model demand is explicit.
opportunities.risks: OpenRouter and the labs may add smart routing; routing quality is hard to prove; thin margins.

opportunities.name: QuotaMeter
opportunities.one_liner: A cross-provider usage meter and forecaster for AI coding subscriptions and API spend.
opportunities.problem: Subscription quotas drain fast and unpredictably, limits change without notice, and users cannot see burn per task or what drained them.
opportunities.target_users: Heavy users of Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Copilot.
opportunities.evidence: T020 (103 findings, 40 tool complaints) and T034 (79 findings, 11 build requests) both describe opaque limits; T057 (54 findings) shows token-hungry models raising per-task cost.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: Headroom menu-bar app, ccusage, switching tools, stacking Max plans.
opportunities.gap: Existing trackers are single-provider and do not forecast, attribute burn to tasks or sessions, or compare plans and models on real usage.
opportunities.mvp: A local app that reads session logs from Claude Code and Codex, shows remaining 5-hour and weekly budget, per-task burn, a forecast of when limits hit, and alerts.
opportunities.why_now: Limits keep changing and new models use far more tokens per task (T057, 14 findings in the last 90 days).
opportunities.risks: Providers may add native meters; relies on log formats that can change; small willingness to pay at individual level.

opportunities.name: SpendGate
opportunities.one_liner: An enterprise LLM gateway with per-employee and per-agent token attribution, caps and forecasting.
opportunities.problem: Companies cannot see, attribute, cap or forecast AI token spend per team or agent, and budgets are exhausted within months.
opportunities.target_users: Engineering leaders, finance teams and CFOs at AI-adopting companies.
opportunities.evidence: T054 has 51 findings across 11 sources with 17 build requests; T083 (50 findings) shows vendors also struggle with usage pricing; T020 cites budget overruns that led Microsoft to cancel licenses.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: Cloudflare AI Gateway budgets, LLM gateways, ccusage, per-employee caps.
opportunities.gap: Gateways meter API calls, but subscription-based coding tools and agent-level attribution with policy enforcement and finance-friendly forecasts are poorly covered.
opportunities.mvp: A proxy plus dashboard that attributes tokens by user, team and agent, sets caps and alerts, and exports chargeback reports, with a connector that ingests Claude Code and Codex usage data.
opportunities.why_now: Enterprise coding-agent budgets are blowing out (#10201, #1991), and CFO-level attention is new.
opportunities.risks: Existing gateway vendors (Cloudflare, LiteLLM, Portkey-type) can add this; enterprise sales cycles are long.

opportunities.name: EvalBench Workbench
opportunities.one_liner: A lightweight workbench for trace annotation, error clustering and auto-drafted private evals, rerun on every new model.
opportunities.problem: Building evals, annotating traces and clustering errors is tedious and fragmented; individuals and companies want private evals to choose models and catch regressions.
opportunities.target_users: AI product teams, agent builders and power users choosing between models.
opportunities.evidence: T012 (99 findings, 15 build requests, 39 in last 90 days), T065 (55 findings, 15 build requests), T082 (49 findings), T040 (83 findings on silent regressions) all request this.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: Braintrust, Promptfoo, LangSmith, Hamel Husain's eval skills, Harbor, custom clustering notebooks.
opportunities.gap: Existing tools assume you already know how to write evals; the skill of turning real tasks and traces into evals, plus a nerf tracker for personal workloads, is underserved.
opportunities.mvp: A web app that ingests traces, lets you annotate in-situ, clusters failures, drafts an eval from each failure class, and reruns the suite against new model versions with a regression chart.
opportunities.why_now: Public benchmarks are saturating, evals are called the bottleneck, and models change silently (#13479, #1220).
opportunities.risks: Crowded by Braintrust and LangSmith; labs may add built-in eval features; requires user data trust.

opportunities.name: Instruction File Manager
opportunities.one_liner: A linter, syncer and token-cost auditor for AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, skills and rules across coding agents.
opportunities.problem: Instruction files go stale, bloat, are ignored and differ across tools, and configuration and skills are not portable when switching agents.
opportunities.target_users: Developers and teams using several coding agents.
opportunities.evidence: T009 (110 findings, 26 workarounds) and T080 (48 findings, 15 build requests) both describe the pain; T056 notes giant AGENTS.md files burn tokens.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: Symlinks, pre-commit linters, hooks, /init and /doctor audits, claude-config repos.
opportunities.gap: No tool diffs and syncs configs across Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, flags stale or conflicting rules, or measures whether a rule changes behavior.
opportunities.mvp: A CLI/VS Code extension that parses all agent config files, generates tool-specific files from one source, flags contradictions and dead rules, and shows token cost per file.
opportunities.why_now: Switching between harnesses is common and newer models perform worse with old hand-holding rules (#2930).
opportunities.risks: Small standalone market; labs may converge on a common AGENTS.md standard; easy to copy.

opportunities.name: Agent Control Tower
opportunities.one_liner: A cross-vendor dashboard for supervising many parallel coding agents with status, notifications and queued reviews.
opportunities.problem: Running many agents across repos and worktrees causes context switching and notification overload, with no single view of what needs attention.
opportunities.target_users: Developers running several coding agents in parallel.
opportunities.evidence: Overlapping themes T029 (116 findings), T032 (75 findings, 13 build requests), T059 (62 findings), T072 (74 findings) show heavy demand and many DIY setups.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: tmux, Git worktrees, Conductor, Vibe Kanban, Superset, Cline Kanban, Gas Town, Emdash, Antigravity Agent Manager.
opportunities.gap: Many tools exist but are tied to one vendor or lack real progress status, interruption triage and review queuing across harnesses.
opportunities.mvp: A local web/TUI app that attaches to agent sessions via hooks, shows working/blocked/done status, manages worktrees, and sends one consolidated notification stream with a review queue.
opportunities.why_now: Parallel agent workflows have gone mainstream; users ask for a common API above harnesses (#21403).
opportunities.risks: Very crowded; vendors build native managers; differentiation is hard.

opportunities.name: CompactGuard
opportunities.one_liner: A context manager that pins instructions, checkpoints decisions and audits compaction summaries for long agent sessions.
opportunities.problem: Long sessions fill the context, and compaction loses constraints, decisions and safety instructions, causing drift or destructive actions.
opportunities.evidence: T011 (98 findings), T050 (66 findings) and T028 (76 findings) cover this; explicit requests include #3628, #20266 and #20425.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: /compact, /clear, handoff files, plan.md notes, fresh sessions, server-side compaction, Jev.
opportunities.gap: Nobody pins non-negotiable rules across compaction, retains retrievable pre-compaction text, or checks summaries for lost or injected instructions.
opportunities.mvp: A harness plugin or proxy that keeps a pinned goals/constraints block, stores raw pre-compaction history searchable by tool call, and diffs the summary against pinned items.
opportunities.why_now: Sessions now run for hours; Anthropic is adding managed compaction (#1190) which indicates a pressing need but also competition.
opportunities.risks: Model labs are improving compaction natively; deep integration with closed harnesses is hard.

opportunities.name: Prompt Injection Firewall
opportunities.one_liner: An agent firewall that scans ingested content, strips hidden instructions and enforces deterministic egress policy.
opportunities.problem: Agents that read untrusted content while holding private data and outbound channels can be hijacked, with no complete defense.
opportunities.target_users: Builders and users of browsing and tool-using agents.
opportunities.evidence: T001 is the top-scoring theme (574.4, 123 findings, 11 sources, 9 build requests); T017 (103 findings) and T016 add related security demand.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: Lockdown Mode, URL allowlists, CSP rules, markdown sanitization, BrowseSafe, classifiers, human approval.
opportunities.gap: Defenses are partial and per-product; there is no drop-in layer that checks content before ingestion, flags lethal-trifecta configurations, and enforces egress outside the model.
opportunities.mvp: A proxy/MCP middleware that sanitizes fetched pages, flags hidden text, audits an agent's tool and data permissions for the lethal trifecta, and blocks outbound calls to non-approved destinations.
opportunities.why_now: Prompt injection incidents are rising with browser agents, and builders explicitly ask for runtime filters (#13647, #24254).
opportunities.risks: No complete defense exists so claims are hard to prove; labs ship classifiers natively; hard to prove value.

opportunities.name: Agent Identity Gateway
opportunities.one_liner: Per-agent identity, scoped revocable credentials, approval routing and audit logs for enterprise agent fleets.
opportunities.problem: Enterprises cannot scope, attribute, audit or revoke agent permissions, and shared credentials widen the blast radius.
opportunities.target_users: Security teams and enterprises deploying fleets of agents.
opportunities.evidence: T016 (69 findings from 13 sources, 34 in the last 90 days, 15 build requests); T019 (81 findings) shows data-governance demand; T049 supports kill-switch needs.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: WorkOS Airlock, per-agent keys, cloud IAM service accounts, scoped credentials, guardrail policies.
opportunities.gap: Cloud IAM is not built for agent-level attribution, approval gates and one-click revocation across frameworks.
opportunities.mvp: A gateway for MCP and API calls that issues per-agent short-lived credentials, logs each call with agent identity, supports approval rules and a kill switch.
opportunities.why_now: Agents now use real logged-in browser profiles (#17955) and enterprises are deploying fleets; interest is recent.
opportunities.risks: Big identity vendors (Okta, WorkOS, cloud providers) will move; long enterprise sales cycles.

opportunities.name: Local Model Fit
opportunities.one_liner: A hardware-aware advisor and launcher that recommends model, quant and settings, and wires up a local coding-agent stack.
opportunities.problem: Open models outgrow consumer hardware, users lack guidance on what fits their machine, and wiring local models to harnesses by hand is brittle.
opportunities.target_users: Developers with consumer GPUs, laptops and Macs who want local or open-weight coding agents.
opportunities.evidence: T014 (89 findings, 21 build requests), T063 (75 findings), T070 (63 findings) all show demand; #14317 asks directly for a tool showing which models a Mac can run.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: LLmFit, hf CLI auto-pick, OpenCode, Roo, Cline, Pi, LM Studio, Ollama Modelfiles, Unsloth guides.
opportunities.gap: Advice is scattered; nothing recommends a tested model plus quant plus harness bundle for your hardware with correct chat templates and tool-calling settings.
opportunities.mvp: A CLI that detects hardware, recommends a tested model/quant/context combination, launches llama-server or Ollama, and configures OpenCode or Claude Code with the correct templates and loop-detection retries.
opportunities.why_now: Mid-size Qwen/Gemma models now make local agents plausible, and 23 T014 findings are recent.
opportunities.risks: Fast-moving model landscape needs constant curation; Ollama and LM Studio may add this; low willingness to pay.

opportunities.name: Agent Memory Layer
opportunities.one_liner: A vendor-neutral, inspectable and editable memory store for agents with consolidation and scoping.
opportunities.problem: Agent memory is siloed in hidden stores, drifts, accumulates contradictions, and cannot be exported or shared across agents and teams.
opportunities.target_users: Developers building agents and users of multiple agent products.
opportunities.evidence: T045 (80 findings, 10 build requests), T071 (43 findings, 17 build requests), T009 (110 findings) with requests such as #5129 and #14486.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: Markdown memory files, Mimir, Supermemory, Honcho, Hyperspell, Notion shared memory, Cognition's open memory format.
opportunities.gap: No agreed architecture or portable format; users can't see or edit what agents remember, nor share scoped memory across vendors.
opportunities.mvp: An MCP server backed by markdown/git storage with nightly consolidation and dedupe, a UI to view and edit memories, and scoping by project, team and user.
opportunities.why_now: Long-running and multi-agent setups make re-explaining context costly (#8124), and open memory formats are emerging.
opportunities.risks: Many funded memory startups; labs build memory natively; standards may fragment.

opportunities.name: Slop Filter
opportunities.one_liner: A cross-platform extension that detects, labels and filters AI-generated content with user tuning.
opportunities.problem: AI-generated posts, comments, books and videos flood feeds, and users cannot tell or filter machine-written content; detectors are unreliable.
opportunities.target_users: Social media, forum and video platform users, and community operators.
opportunities.evidence: T037 (67 findings, 25 build requests), T022 (77 findings, 18 build requests), T043 (71 findings, 14 build requests on detection and provenance).
opportunities.existing_alternatives: Pangram, hn-ai.org, hcker.news, Lobste.rs tags, block lists, Invidious, channel whitelisting, Turnstile.
opportunities.gap: Detectors give false positives and no honest confidence; no tool combines labeling, user-tuned filtering and community moderation controls across platforms.
opportunities.mvp: A browser extension for HN, YouTube and Bluesky that scores items with a detector API, shows confidence, and lets users hide or tag items with a community-shared allowlist and blocklist.
opportunities.why_now: Slop complaints are widespread and recent, and Substack and Steam are being asked for AI filters (#24195, #13569).
opportunities.risks: Detector accuracy limits; platforms may ban scraping or add native labels; arms race with evasion; weak monetization.

opportunities.name: Reward-Hack Auditor
opportunities.one_liner: A detector and auditor for reward hacking, broken benchmark items and suspicious score jumps in evals and RL environments.
opportunities.problem: Agents exploit flawed graders and environments, and benchmarks contain broken tasks and buggy verifiers, so scores misstate ability.
opportunities.target_users: Eval builders, RL environment designers and benchmark maintainers.
opportunities.evidence: T025 (79 findings, 38 in the last 90 days, 14 build requests), T076 (43 findings), T039 (69 findings on hidden harness details), T006 (107 findings on benchmark distrust).
opportunities.existing_alternatives: LLM transcript graders, canary reward paths, activation probes, CheatBench, Epoch audits, Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index.
opportunities.gap: Detection is one-off and manual; no tool audits an environment before training or flags impossible tasks, leaky items and anomalous score jumps.
opportunities.mvp: A service that ingests eval transcripts and task sets, flags impossible or leaky tasks, detects suspicious shortcuts using transcript grading, and reports corrected scores with recorded harness settings.
opportunities.why_now: Reward hacking incidents are frequent in recent months and labs publicly ask for such tools (#18, #4086).
opportunities.risks: Narrow buyer set (labs, eval companies); labs may build in-house; needs credibility.

opportunities.name: Defender Access Gateway
opportunities.one_liner: A vetted gateway giving security defenders verified access to strong models with audit logs and fallback routing.
opportunities.problem: Hosted models refuse incident response and malware analysis tasks, and trusted-access programs are slow, pushing defenders toward weaker open models while attackers speed up.
opportunities.target_users: Security defenders, incident responders, SOC teams and under-resourced organizations.
opportunities.evidence: T015 (87 findings, 10 build requests) and T018 (88 findings from 13 sources, 16 build requests) describe both access friction and the need for automated patching.
opportunities.existing_alternatives: Trusted Access for Cyber, Project Glasswing, GPT-5.4-Cyber, Claude Code Security, Codex Security, self-hosted GLM, Persona ID verification.
opportunities.gap: Labs' programs are gated and slow; small defenders lack a unified, verified service combining model access, scanning, triage and patch suggestions.
opportunities.mvp: A service for verified security teams that routes defensive prompts to permitted models or hosted open-weight cyber models, logs usage for audit, and provides agentic scan-triage-patch templates.
opportunities.why_now: Defenders report refusals as a blocker (#19978, #10800), and AI-driven attack speed is rising (#24636).
